_comment: THROWAWAY POSITIVE-CONTROL BRANCH — deliberately wrong. Never merge. Induces drift(ict-trainer-vm ocpus 1->2) + missing/undeclared (gateway renamed) to prove --fail-on-drift can actually go red against the real cloud.
_seeded_from: Live report run 32128150842 (region eu-paris-1): 3 instances, all VM.Standard.A1.Flex, all RUNNING, totalling 4 OCPU / 24 GB.
_provenance_note: ict-ib-gateway and ict-trainer-vm were read verbatim from that run. The live-trader row is DERIVED: the run's totals (3 instances / 4 OCPU / 24 GB) leave exactly 2 OCPU / 12 GB for the third, and CLAUDE.md documents the live trader as ict-bot-arm at that exact shape. If the display_name is wrong, the next report run reports it as missing + undeclared rather than match — which is the tool working, not failing. Correct it there if so.

instances.role: Live trader — ict-trader-live.service + ict-web-api.service. Money at risk. Migrated off the x86 micro 2026-06-14.
Training centre — ML lifecycle (datasets, training, registry, eval). No live trade authority.
IB Gateway (Java/Xvfb/IBC) on its own box — isolated off the money VM after the 2026-06-10 wedge cascade.

_budget_note: 4 OCPU / 24 GB total — EXACTLY the legacy/PAYG Always Free ceiling, and DOUBLE the 2 OCPU / 12 GB ceiling Oracle imposed on Always Free tenancies from 2026-06-15. There is ZERO Ampere headroom: any additional A1.Flex instance would exceed the legacy ceiling too. Nothing has been shut down in the two months since the change and the operator reports a card on file with no charges, which is consistent with an upgraded/PAYG tenancy retaining 4/24 — but the account type is visible only in the OCI console and this file does not assert it.
